notes: The river is currently at 8,000 CFS at the top end, the clarity is excellent, and we have some clouds and sprinkles over the next three days. And if you know what's up, this can make for a great day on the Sac! Big BWO hatches are happening in the late afternoon, midges in the morning. The caddis may or may not be happening, be prepared either way.

Typically with stormy weather and lighter winds it's a mayfly op, but some off-brands of caddis, like Glossosomas and Brachycentrus, can make their appearance. Up top you will want to fish the BP Weiss Nymph, Jig nation in BWO, Olive Hotspot, Rubberlegs, and Jigged Bird's Nests. Lower in the river Rubberlegs, Peaches 'n Cream, Ginger Snap, Eng Thing, Olive Hotspot, Cinnamon Fox Poopahs, and Bird's Nests are good choices. Swing soft hackles or a dark Missing Link in last half hour of light.

hatches.fallback: No hatch listed. Swing soft hackles or a dark Missing Link.

water.name: Fall River

notes: With the storms rolling in this week, this could be 'The Place' to be! When it's cloudy and stormy, the hatches can be epic. And there are more hatches overall the past week with PMDs being the main hatch. It is fishing well, the weeds are choking the bridges and the guides are working to open up lanes to get through. Smaller nymphs on a dry-dropper rig or swung are doing the most work. Tricos are still coming off and you can get a spinner fall in the super early mornings. Good dropper flies are Jim Nations, BP Weiss Nypmhs, Sweet Peas, Two-Bit Hookers, Red Micro Mays, and Russ' Sin City. For dries, the smaller Rusty Spinners, PMD Challenged and PMD Hackle Stackers, presented correctly, will get fish. Strip Pine Squirrel Leeches and Water Boatmen in the mid-day and afternoons. September is a great time to fish the Fall. If you would like to set up a day on the Fall, give a call Bryan in Outfitters at 800-669-3474 to set up a trip!

With storms rolling in and the weather cooling, the Blue Wing Olives and midges should be pouring off. Look for rising fish in the flats, the riffles below the Hwy 299 bridge will yield fish on Rubberlegs and Golden Stone nymphs. Dry-dropper rigs will allow you to pick up a fish or two on the dry, BP Weiss and the Weiss Firefly, Olive Hotspots, Sweet Peas, Zebra Midges and anything #18 or smaller is the name of the game for a dropper there. Bring the small dries, #18 - 22 Adams, and any Baetis dries you have. BWO nymphs to bring are the Sweet Pea, Zack's BWO Jig Nation, Olive S&M, Black Micro May, Rubberlegs, and whatever is jammed in the fly cup stuffed on the bottom of your pack - sometimes on Hat you get the inside slider when you're looking for the fastball. Hat Creek is fun in the fall!

The river is definitely showing signs from the last storm and we will see big flows and probably colored water over the next few weeks. The upper river will probably see some more fish coming through, and we hope, up into Oregon! If you are fishing, swing low and slow for best success. We're looking forward to June when the halfpounders and early summer run fish show up!

water.name: McCloud River

notes: To close the chapter on the bear thing in the Conservancy, we heard someone sprayed the bear which we hope will deter them from interacting with humans in the future. Good reports coming in on the angling still, and the storms this week should stir up the pot hatch-wise. Clarity is excellent and the temps are holding in the upper river. Overall the river is fishing well, best before and after the sun is on the water. Look to see more browns in the river as they get ready to spawn this fall. Dry-dropper with a Chubby Chernobyl hanging a Weiss Firefly, Walt's Worm, Olive Hotspot, or Sweet Pea is a good setup. The Yellow Sallies are coming off in the afternoons, so swap your dropper with a UV Sally or Jiggy Yellow Sally. The Browns are moving up from the lake into the upper section of the river as they ready to spawn, so streamer fishing can get you hooked up to a big one. To reserve a day with one of our expert guides to experience one of the most picturesque streams in the north state, call Bryan in Outfitters at 800-669-3474.

The latest news on the Pit is the clarity is good, flows are where they should be, and the temps are not too warm for the fish in Pit 3 and 4. Fishing has been good as well with nymphs & Euronymph set ups. The fish will clump up in the drainages with cold seeps/creek mouths. Keep a thermometer handy and call it quits when you get readings above 65 F. Good flies are always Perdigons, Hotspots, Rubberlegs, and don't discount a well-fished crayfish pattern. Some people fish Woolly Buggers, TJ Hookers can be very effective. The fall will be a good one on the Pit! This is a great river to fish a Euro rod and we highly recommend it. Be careful though, this can be a slippery river to wade. We recommend a wading staff when fishing the Pit. Be aware that the flows on the Pit can and will change without notice, so definitely check before you go! And be prepared to get out when the river begins to rise. Here are some useful links to monitor the flows: Pit 3 - Below Pit 3 Dam Pit 5 - Through Big Bend

The1,200 CFS flows will continue through September 21st. The restoration channel below the Cemetery Hole was adding turbidity to the river yesterday, it is now cleared up below it with 4+ foot visibility. Fish are stacking in around Junction City. This flow bump should bring fish up that have been holding below Cedar Flat, expect a push of new summers coming into the Juction City area soon. Now would be a great time to swing one up below Pigeon Point. A lot of salmon have piled into holes in the upper river pushing fish into other areas to hold, so keep that in mind. We have quite a few fish in the 18-22" range from Lewiston on downstream with a few large adults thrown in the mix. Fish are pretty grabby right now, it is a good time to swing and skate. For now, the water temps at Hoopa are below 67 F and with the clouds and rain we will see, they should drop further. We've got guides available right now that can get you out, give us a call or you can go directly to our Trinity guide page and book a trip now. For good reason! The learning curve can be quite steep learning when and where to go, and what type of water to target. notes: Temps on the lower end of the river have decreased over the past week and are now touching the underside of 67 F. No solid reports from anyone fishing, but generally fishing above around Dunsmuir should be solid. With the storms this week you should see epic BWO and midge hatches, bring your dry box! This is little black bug season on the Upper, so Zebras in #18 or smaller, BP Weiss nymphs, black S&Ms, black Micro Mays and any other teeny, tiny nymph chucked into the frothy stuff is the best tactic during the day. Midges are always a good idea to fish. Towards dark you can head hunt with smaller dark Missing links and Adams. The browns are moving up the river from the lake, so bring a streamer rod. Always have Rubberlegs, Perdigons, BP Weiss Nymphs, Poopahs, Zebra Midges and Bird's Nests to round out your offerings. Upper Sacramento Flows at Delta
